title: Minimum Flips for Bitwise OR
description: Given three positive integers `a`, `b`, and `c`, return the minimum number of single-bit flips required in the binary representations of `a` and `b` so that `(a | b) == c`. A flip changes a single bit from `0` to `1` or from `1` to `0`.
hints: Inspect each bit independently: `(a | b) ^ c` identifies every bit position where `a | b` differs from `c`.
Every mismatching bit needs 1 flip, except when `c` has bit `0` while both `a` and `b` have bit `1`, which requires 2 flips.

examples.explanation: Flipping 2 (0010) to 1 (0001) and 6 (0110) to 4 (0100) takes 3 flips so 1 | 4 == 5.
Flipping bit 0 of 4 (0100) to 5 (0101) takes 1 flip so 5 | 2 == 7.
1 | 2 already equals 3, so 0 flips are needed.
